title: Floating-Point Numbers & Rounding Errors
description: Machine numbers, IEEE 754, machine epsilon, absolute and relative errors, cancellation.
html:
🔢 Floating-Point Numbers & Rounding Errors

1. Machine Numbers

$$x = \pm\, d_0.d_1\ldots d_{t-1} \cdot b^{e}, \qquad d_0 \neq 0$$

Base $b$, mantissa length $t$, fixed exponent range. There are only finitely many machine numbers; their spacing grows with the magnitude.

IEEE 754 double

$t = 53$, $\varepsilon_{\text{mach}} = 2^{-52} \approx 2.2 \cdot 10^{-16}$, $u = 2^{-53} \approx 1.1 \cdot 10^{-16}$. Largest number $\approx 1.8 \cdot 10^{308}$ (overflow), smallest normalised $\approx 2.2 \cdot 10^{-308}$ (underflow).

2. Rounding and Error Measures

$$\mathrm{fl}(x) = x(1+\varepsilon), \quad |\varepsilon| \le u, \qquad \mathrm{fl}(x \circ y) = (x \circ y)(1 + \varepsilon)$$

$$\text{absolute: } |\tilde x - x|, \qquad \text{relative: } \frac{|\tilde x - x|}{|x|}$$

3. Cancellation

Subtracting nearly equal numbers amplifies existing errors: only a few valid digits remain. It does not create a new error, it makes old ones visible.

Example

$$x^2 - 10^8 x + 1 = 0: \quad \text{naive } x_2 = 7.45\cdot10^{-9}, \ \text{correct } 1.0\cdot 10^{-8}$$

4. Remedies

  • Vieta: compute $x_1$ without subtraction, then $x_2 = c/(a x_1)$.
  • Conjugate: $\sqrt{x+1} - \sqrt{x} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x+1} + \sqrt{x}}$.
  • Identities: $1 - \cos x = 2\sin^2\frac{x}{2}$, $e^x - 1 = x + \frac{x^2}{2} + \dots$.
  • Summation: small numbers first, Kahan summation, logarithms for products.

5. Typical Mistakes

  • Confusing $\varepsilon_{\text{mach}}$ with the smallest positive number.
  • Regarding cancellation as a “rounding error of the subtraction” – the subtraction is exact.
  • Assuming associativity in floating point.
